_meta.indication: DOJOLVI is indicated as a source of calories and fatty acids for the treatment of pediatric and adult patients with molecularly confirmed long-chain fatty acid oxidation disorders (LC-FAOD).

pivotal_trials.design: Active-comparator, 1:1 randomized, double-blind trial comparing food-grade triheptanoin (C7) to purified trioctanoin (C8) at a target dose of 20% DCI over 4 months (patients were instructed to consume 20% DCI but actually took 11% to 22% DCI); 32 treated at 2 U.S. centers
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with confirmed LC-FAOD (CPT-2, VLCAD, or LCHAD and/or TFP deficiency) aged 7 years or older with a history of at least one episode of rhabdomyolysis, stable on a diet using MCT oil; ages 7 to 64 years
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Prespecified primary endpoints were cardiac function (ECHO), total energy expenditure, and treadmill exercise testing (an exploratory primary endpoint); secondary was incidence of rhabdomyolysis
pivotal_trials.result: After 4 months, no clinically meaningful differences were observed between the two treatment groups in metabolic hospitalizations, cardiac function on resting echocardiogram and treadmill ergometry, or metabolic biomarkers; the lack of clinically meaningful differences provided qualitative evidence of efficacy for triheptanoin as an alternative source of MCT oil

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%) are gastrointestinal: abdominal pain [60%], diarrhea [44%], vomiting [44%], and nausea [14%]; GI adverse reactions led to dose reductions in 35% and 12% of patients in Study 1 and Study 2, respectively
target_moa: Triheptanoin is a medium-chain triglyceride (MCT oil providing 8.3 kcal/mL) whose metabolite heptanoate provides acetyl-CoA and propionyl-CoA anaplerotic substrates for the TCA cycle, replacing energy substrates that LC-FAOD patients cannot generate from long-chain fatty acids
modality: Small molecule (medium-chain triglyceride / triglyceride of heptanoic acid; oral liquid, 100% w/w triheptanoin)

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee was not held for this application.

summary.text: Triheptanoin (Dojolvi) was submitted as a 505(b)(2) NDA on July 31, 2019 and approved June 30, 2020 as a standard review. It held orphan drug designation (April 15, 2015), Fast Track designation (March 7, 2019), and rare pediatric disease designation (March 28, 2019); breakthrough designation had been denied in 2017. It was not an accelerated approval and no advisory committee was held.

requirement.text: PMR 3858-1: Conduct a worldwide, single-arm, pregnancy safety study in women exposed to Dojolvi during pregnancy to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications, adverse effects on the developing fetus and neonate, and adverse effects on the infant; infant outcomes assessed through at least the first year of life

citations.quote: 3858-1 Conduct a worldwide, single-arm, pregnancy safety study in women exposed to Dojolvi during pregnancy to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications, adverse effects on the developing fetus and neonate, and adverse effects on the infant. Infant outcomes will be assessed through at least the first year of life. Results will be analyzed and reported descriptively.
